editorial.hero_description: Your adventure basecamp beside Rincón de la Vieja's volcanoes and hot springs.
editorial.description: A family-friendly ranch hotel set in the dry tropical forest beside Rincón de la Vieja National Park, offering comfortable rooms and a huge lineup of on-site adventure tours. Guests enjoy complimentary access to waterfalls and the Río Negro hot springs.

why_stay_here.title: Why Stay Here
why_stay_here.summary: Hotel Hacienda Guachipelín is one of the best places to stay if you want to combine comfort with unforgettable experiences around Guanacaste.

luxury.reason: identity.luxury_level is Standard, the lowest tier; description emphasizes comfortable rather than upscale rooms.

families.reason: Active Families profile: reviewers traveled with kids and teens and enjoyed free access to hot springs, waterfalls and activities on property.

couples.reason: No couples/honeymoon profile; entirely adventure and family-framed.

wellness.reason: Simbiosis Spa and volcanic mud baths, plus complimentary hot springs access.

adventure_access.reason: On-site adventure center with zip lining, tubing, rappelling and canyoning; Adventure Seekers profile calls it a one-stop basecamp.

wild_insights.local_take: Ideal for active travelers and families who want zip lining, tubing, and hot springs right outside their door — and reassuring for celiac guests, since the whole kitchen is gluten-free.

faq.q: What activities are included for hotel guests?
faq.a: Guests receive complimentary access to 7 waterfalls and the Río Negro hot springs, plus scenic hikes and the pool, with adventure tours like zip lining and tubing available on site.

faq.q: Where is Hotel Hacienda Guachipelín located?
faq.a: The hotel is located next to Rincón de la Vieja National Park, about 25 km northeast of Liberia in Guanacaste, roughly 45 minutes to an hour from Liberia Airport (LIR).

faq.q: Is the food safe for celiac and gluten-free guests?
faq.a: Yes — the on-site La Hacienda Restaurant is 100% gluten-free, with locally sourced, farm-to-table dishes crafted from traditional Guanacaste recipes.
